sentence: This project tries to use alternative splicing to control where and how strongly gene therapies switch on their cargoes.
This project studies how the brain balances mental flexibility and stability in working memory, looking at circuits, cells and synapses.
This project tests whether viral DNA joining the human genome helps cervical cells grow into expanded groups of altered cells and cancer.
This project grows human leukemia cells inside fragments of bone marrow to study blood diseases and develop more effective treatments.
This project uses a rodent model of cocaine addiction to find out how the prefrontal cortex can be changed to reduce relapse.
This project tries to target all arms of the immune system so it can eliminate cells infected with HIV.
This project tries to find out how influenza A viruses successfully infect a single host, to improve infection control.
This project studies which proteins make up the paranodal junction, where the myelin sheath anchors to the axon, to help axons repair after injuries.
This project studies how a type of immune cell takes up and presents pieces of viruses and tumors, focusing on one protein.
This project studies normal and abnormal human development using stem cells.
This project builds a remote screening tool that combines maternal reports with computer analysis of infant behavior to predict later behavior problems.
This project offers a central core of tools for studying metabolism, including computer analysis, gene editing and metabolic tests in cells and mouse models.
This project studies how symptom-free carriers, infections brought in from nearby countries and host immunity affect malaria spread in northwest Ecuador.
This project studies how disrupted protein regulation in the kidney relates to acute kidney injury, looking for key molecules that drugs could target.
This project studies families with inherited osteoarthritis to find genes that raise risk, then tests how those genes change function in mouse models.
This project switches off one extra copy of chromosome 21 in three-dimensional nerve cell cultures to see how the extra copy changes brain cells.
This project uses monkeys infected with modified viruses to study how antibodies against HIV develop, aiming to design an immunization scheme.
This project studies how a transcription factor works within chromatin and tests its role in a mouse model of multiple sclerosis.
This project designs proteins from scratch that bind metal cofactors, to learn how protein structure controls the function of metalloenzymes.
This project tries to improve child health research by supporting pediatric physician-scientists.
